title: Monolith Dynamics Systems
text:
Monolith Dynamics Systems

notes:
Short summary: Large industrial automation vendor evaluating Redwood Dedicated for multi-site chat/code-assistant and low-latency reranking across global control centers. Primary ask: reserved capacity with deterministic throughput and priority lanes to protect latency-sensitive routes. Interested in traffic shaping (per-route quotas, token-based priority lanes), tenant isolation guarantees, noisy-neighbor mitigation (CPU/GPU QoS + scheduling), and clear SLOs/SLA credit policy. Procurement wants predictable cost via reserved GPUs and a defined upgrade path for bursts. Security: VPC-only control plane, enterprise KMS, SOC2, SSO integration, EU data residency for EU plants. AE notes: customer repeatedly asked "How do you guarantee p95 for critical routes during large batch jobs?". SE note: request for microbench (8-H100 pool simulation) + network isolation test. Legal: pushing for 99.95% uptime and extended credits for degradation longer than 30m.

next_step:
Run 2-week Dedicated POC with traffic shaping tests; schedule capacity sizing workshop; send draft SOW.

blockers:
legal SLA language for uptime/credits
network egress rules for VPC peering
budget approval for reserved GPUs
need concrete noisy-neighbor mitigation evidence

priority_requirements:
p95_latency_chat<120ms
sustained_throughput:500rps
burst_capacity:2000rps_for_60s
reserved_gpus:8-H100
per-route_quota:critical=70% tokens, background=30% tokens

technical_questions_outstanding:
Exact SLA credit calculation for multi-zone outages
How is KV-cache isolation enforced between tenants?
Can we enforce per-route GPU QoS (noisy neighbor throttling)?
Network egress requirements for private control plane in customer VPC

recommended_next_steps_from_redwood:
Schedule capacity-sizing workshop week of 2026-03-22; provision 8xH100 dry-run cluster for 48h internal load test; create POC plan and SOW; engage solutions architect to produce traffic-shaping runbook.

activity_timeline:
2026-02-18: Intro call (Jordan) - discovered primary pain: unpredictable tail latency when customers run large embedding/rerank jobs against control-center data.
2026-02-25: Technical deep-dive (Maya) - discussed reserved GPU sizing, kernel selection, quantization trade-offs; sketched priority-lane approach (route tags + token budgets).
2026-03-02: Onsite workshop + Fireflies (ff_20260302_9012) - ran baseline throughput targets; identified noisy-neighbor scenario when nightly bulk embedding jobs coincide with business-hour chat traffic.
2026-03-05: Procurement/Legal kickoff - customer requested SLA draft and list of mitigations for tenant isolation; asked for formal SLO language for p50/p95/p99 latencies per-route.
2026-03-08: AE sent initial proposal - recommends 8x H100 reserved pool, 2-tier priority lanes (critical vs background), automated traffic shaping rules, and 2-week POC to validate SLOs under synthetic load.
2026-03-10: SE follow-up - provided sample config for per-route quotas, suggested fallback routes to smaller quantized model for background traffic.

customer_quotes:
We need hard guarantees for our operator-facing chat — anything over 150ms p95 is noticeable.
If background batch jobs can impact chat, this is a non-starter.
